newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees decline in number of drug addicts.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees decline in number of drug addicts.

text.p: Singapore has seen a drop in the number of drug addicts arrested over the last two years thanks to more vigorous law enforcement and more effective treatment programmes, a government official said on Thursday.
The total number of addicts arrested fell to 6,065 in 1995 from 6,165 in 1994, said Ho Peng Kee, senior parliamentary secretary for law and home affairs.
The first half of 1996 saw a further decline in the number of addicts arrested to 2,744 from 3,025 in the second half of 1995, Ho said at the opening of a counselling centre.
He said the number of new addicts dropped sharply to 978 in 1995 from 1,341 in 1994 while the relapse rate among recovering addicts dipped to 77.5 percent from a high of 81 percent in 1994.
Ho said the government recognised the importance of counselling and support services in protecting recovering addicts from a relapse.
He said Singapore needed more professional full-time drug counsellors as the pool of about 380 volunteers was severely stretched counselling over 9,000 recovering addicts.
Singapore has a mandatory death sentence for people convicted of possessing more than 15 grams (half an ounce) of heroin, 30 grams (an ounce) of morphine or 500 grams (18 ounces) of cannabis.
